cards.name: Transform Again
cards.summary: Repeats the most recent transformation (move, scale, rotate, reflect, shear or a Transform Each setting, including whether it made a copy) on the current selection with exactly the same values. Pressed again and again it keeps stepping, so one rotated or moved copy becomes an evenly spaced series.
use_for: radial artwork: rotate a copy around a set pivot once, then repeat for clock ticks, sunbursts, petals or gear teeth
evenly spaced rows of icons, dashes, stripes or grid lines (move a copy once, repeat)
giving the next object the same scale or rotation you just applied to another
avoid: arrays you will want to respace or recount later: the copies are separate objects; use Effect > Distort & Transform > Transform or a Repeat (radial / grid) object for an editable series
spacing that should vary: every repeat uses identical values
nothing selected or no transformation yet in the session: there is nothing to repeat
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("transformagain") (confirmed: same result as the menu item). Object-model alternative (unverified): call the same PageItem.translate / resize / rotate again yourself.

review.changes: script_api: marked the untested object-model alternative (unverified)

cards.name: Transform Each...
cards.summary: Opens the Transform Each dialog, which scales, moves, rotates and reflects every selected object around its own reference point rather than around the selection as a whole, optionally with a random amount per object, and can apply the result to copies.
cards.how: Select the objects (it also works on a single object). Set Scale Horizontal / Vertical (%), Move Horizontal / Vertical and the Rotate angle; tick Reflect X or Reflect Y; pick the reference point on the locator (centre keeps each object in place). Random varies each object between zero and the entered values. Options: Scale Corners, Scale Strokes & Effects, Transform Objects / Transform Patterns. Turn on Preview, then OK, or Copy to transform duplicates and keep the originals.
use_for: shrinking or rotating a scatter of icons, stars or confetti in place without pulling them toward the centre
random jitter of size, angle and position across repeated shapes for an organic pattern
turning every letter outline or tile by the same angle around its own centre
avoid: objects that should transform as one unit keeping their layout: use Object > Transform > Scale / Rotate or the bounding box
grouped artwork: a group counts as one object, so ungroup first if each piece should move on its own
repeatable random results: Random gives a different outcome on every run
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Transform v23") opens the Transform Each dialog (confirmed; the shortcut-file id "Transform3" fails with Error 1200 in 30.2.1). Object-model equivalent (unverified): loop over app.activeDocument.selection and call item.resize(sx, sy, true, true, true, true, lineScale, Transformation.CENTER), item.rotate(angle, true, true, true, true, Transformation.CENTER) and item.translate(dx, dy) on each item.

review.changes: how: 'two or more objects' was wrong (it works on one object too) and the number is not in the batch; how: dropped the unharvested '9-point' count

cards.name: Ungroup
cards.summary: Removes one level of grouping from the selected group(s): the group's direct members become separately selectable objects, while groups nested inside stay grouped. Ungrouping a clipping group also releases the clip, leaving the clipping path as an unpainted path.
use_for: editing one element of grouped artwork such as an imported logo, icon set or PDF
breaking a pasted or traced graphic into parts to recolour or rearrange them
separating pieces before sending them to their own layers for export or animation
avoid: groups that carry their own effects, opacity or graphic style: those group-level attributes are lost; edit inside the group in Isolation Mode (double-click) instead
clipping groups you still need: select inside with the Direct Selection tool or isolate rather than ungrouping
deeply nested groups: one level per press; use Ungroup All to flatten everything
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("ungroup") (id paired with the default shortcut set, not confirmed by execution). Object-model alternative (unverified): move each member out with item.move(group, ElementPlacement.PLACEBEFORE), then remove the empty GroupItem.

review.changes: none (summary, use_for, avoid, status, scriptable, script_api id, shortcut and equivalents checked against the batch and pgd.py items)

cards.name: Ungroup All
cards.summary: Dissolves grouping completely in one step, nested groups included, so only individual objects remain (Ungroup removes one level at a time). Read from the name, menu place and shortcut only: the harvest did not execute it, so whether it works on the selection or on the whole document, and how it treats clipping groups inside, is unverified.
use_for: flattening deeply nested groups in imported PDF, EPS or SVG artwork before editing
cleaning a clipart or icon file so every shape can be recoloured or moved on its own
avoid: artwork whose groups carry effects, opacity or clipping masks you need: ungroup selectively with Ungroup or edit in Isolation Mode
files whose group structure organises layers for later edits, export or animation
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("ungroupAll") (id paired with the default shortcut set, not confirmed by execution).

cards.name: Unlock All
cards.summary: Unlocks every locked object in the document at once and leaves the freshly unlocked objects selected. Layer locks set in the Layers panel are a separate lock and are not changed.
use_for: freeing a locked background, template image or guide shape once the layout is done
finding everything that was locked earlier: it arrives selected
opening up a received file whose objects were locked by someone else
avoid: freeing a single object: click its lock icon in the Layers panel instead
pressing Delete or moving straight afterwards: the unlocked objects are now part of the selection
objects on a locked layer: unlock the layer in the Layers panel
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("unlockAll") (id paired with the default shortcut set, not confirmed by execution). Object-model alternative (unverified): set item.locked = false for each item in app.activeDocument.pageItems.

review.changes: none (summary, use_for, avoid, status, scriptable, script_api id, shortcut and equivalents checked against the batch and pgd.py items)

cards.name: Copy (Secondary)
cards.summary: A second keyboard slot for Edit > Copy with no menu entry of its own (listed under Other Misc in Keyboard Shortcuts): F3 copies the selected artwork, or selected text while typing, to the clipboard and leaves it in place, the same as the primary Copy.
use_for: one-hand copy on the function-key row (F2 cut, F3 copy, F4 paste) during repetitive layout
a second, remappable copy key in a custom shortcut set
avoid: scripts: call app.copy() or the primary Copy command, not the secondary slot
duplicating in place: a plain Paste after copying lands centred in the view, so use Paste in Front / Paste in Back / Paste in Place, or Alt-drag

cards.name: Subscript (Secondary)
cards.summary: Alternate shortcut, active only while editing type, that sets the selected characters to subscript: they shrink and drop below the baseline, as with the Character panel's subscript option. Size and offset come from Document Setup's subscript settings.
use_for: the lowered numerals in chemical formulas on packaging, posters and infographics
index or footnote markers set below the line
avoid: fonts with drawn subscript figures: the synthesized version is a scaled copy of the normal glyph; use the Subscript / Inferior position in the OpenType panel (Window > Type > OpenType) for better-weighted figures
anything outside text editing: the shortcut works only with characters selected in a type object
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("~subscript2") (id from Illustrator Defaults.kys, not confirmed by execution). Object-model equivalent (unverified): textRange.characterAttributes.baselinePosition = FontBaselineOption.SUBSCRIPT.

review.changes: use_for: dropped example digits not in the batch; avoid: the OpenType subscript/inferior position lives in the OpenType panel, not the Character panel

avoid: fonts with drawn superior figures: the synthesized version is a scaled copy of the normal glyph; use the Superscript / Superior position in the OpenType panel (Window > Type > OpenType) for better-weighted figures
anything outside text editing: the shortcut works only with characters selected in a type object
